title: AuthorizationResponse
description: A SUCCESSFUL authorization response is a redirect, not a body. The endpoint answers 302 with a Location header carrying the code; the JSON object below is the query-parameter set inside that Location, and identity_oidc::response::AuthorizationResponse is the type that builds it. There is no route that emits this object as a JSON response body. The 501 envelope is the only body a DEFERRED authorize route produces today (see not-implemented-envelope.schema.json).
x-serde-status: the type is IMPLEMENTED as a shape; the endpoint that would emit the redirect is DEFERRED to phase 4 (OIDC provider)
x-wire-form: the query parameters of the 302 Location header, built by AuthorizationResponse::location

code.description: The authorization code. Single-use, short-lived, and bound to the redirect_uri and PKCE challenge it was issued against. URL-encoded into the Location by AuthorizationResponse::location.

state.description: The state echoed from the request, present because the client's own check depends on it. URL-encoded: a state carrying '&' and unencoded would make the client parse the wrong parameters back.

iss.description: The iss parameter of RFC 9207, which mitigates mix-up attacks in a multi-provider setup. Always this provider's issuer, and identical to the discovery document's 'issuer'. URL-encoded into the Location.

x-rename.note: NOT a serde rename. The Rust field is `issuer` and serde serialises it as `issuer`; `iss` is the name AuthorizationResponse::location writes into the query string. The ID token's own claim is a different type (IdTokenClaims.iss) and is also spelled `iss` on the wire because that struct's Rust field is already named `iss`.

x-location-form.encoding: each of code, state and iss is passed through urlencoding::encode
